prompt: Hypothetical. After five losses in a row, someone says: "A win is due now." Which response is correct?

options.text: Yes, a win is due after five losses
No. In the simple model here, each trade has the same chance, so the losses do not make a win due
Yes, if I wait an hour before the next trade
Only after six losses is a win due

explanations.a: This is the gambler's fallacy. The losses before do not change the chance of the next trade in the simple model.
explanations.c: Waiting does not change the chance. The timing has no effect in this model.
explanations.d: The count does not change the chance either. Six losses are not a signal that a win is due.

prompt: Hypothetical. At a 40% win rate, the chance of a loss on one trade is 0.6. What is the chance of four losses in a row, starting at one given trade? Give the answer as a decimal to four places.
Hypothetical. Four losses in a row, at 1R of Rs 500 each. What is the total loss in rupees?
solution: 4 x Rs 500 = Rs 2,000. As a share of Rs 50,000 that is 2,000 / 50,000 = 4%.

prompt: Hypothetical. At a 40% win rate, which statement about losing streaks is correct?

options.text: I will never see six losses in a row
Six losses in a row can happen. From one given trade, the chance is about 4.7%
Six losses in a row means the method is broken
Six losses in a row are impossible if the plan is good

explanations.a: A 40% win rate does not rule out six losses. It makes them less common than at a lower win rate, but they can still happen.
explanations.c: A streak alone does not prove the method is broken. The simple model says runs happen by chance.
explanations.d: A good plan cannot stop a run of losses. It only sets what you do during one.

prompt: Hypothetical. You say: "I will decide what to do when I am in the streak." Which response is correct?

options.text: Correct, because I will know my feelings at that time
Wrong. The action for each stage is written before the run begins
Correct, for experienced traders only
Correct, if the streak is short

explanations.a: Feelings are strongest in a streak. That is why the action is set before it starts.
explanations.c: Every level of trader can feel pressure in a streak. The pre-set action helps all of them.
explanations.d: You cannot tell in advance how long a streak will last, so the action must already be written.

prompt: Hypothetical. A losing streak reaches your weekly limit on day three. Your plan says: weekly limit reached means stop for the week. What fits the plan?

options.text: Trade on day four at the same size, to win back the loss
Stop for the week as the plan says, and write your feelings in the log
Double the size on day four
Skip the journal, because the week is already lost

explanations.a: Trading again at the same size breaks the weekly limit rule. The plan says to stop for the week.
explanations.c: A bigger size after a loss breaks the no-increase rule and makes the loss harder to recover.
explanations.d: The journal is most useful in a streak. It records the feelings and the rule that was followed.

prompt: Hypothetical journal note: "I doubled my size after four losses to recover faster." Which part of this note is the mistake?

options.text: Wanting to recover faster
Doubling size is not a planned action for this stage, because size stays fixed in a drawdown
Keeping a feelings log
Watching a streak simulator

explanations.a: Wanting to recover is a normal feeling. The mistake is the action that follows from it.
explanations.c: A feelings log is a useful tool. It is not the mistake here.
explanations.d: Simulators help you learn the odds. The mistake is the doubled size after the losses.
